newsitem.title: USA: Alliance Entertainment files reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Alliance Entertainment files reorganization plan.

text.p: Alliance Entertainment Corp, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization Monday, sending jitters through the music industry.

Alliance, which distributes music for hundreds of independent labels, last August named Al Teller, former chairman and chief executive officer of MCA Music Entertainment Group, as Alliance's co-chairman and chief executive officer.

At the time of Teller's appointment, New York-based Alliance had designs on becoming the seventh major music company. The six major music labels are Time Warner Inc., EMI Group Plc, Bertelsmann AG, PolyGram, Seagram Co. Ltd. and Sony Corp.

"The great benefit of having Alliance is that it filled a void in the marketplace. It allowed for a uniform distribution for independent labels that didn't wish or weren't able to go through the large, multinational record company distributors," said Thomas White, a music publishing industry consultant.

But Teller said he expects daily operations of the filing entities will continue uninterrupted, and that those businesses will proceed with substantially more liquidity than has been available in recent months.

He also said he expects employees of the filing entities will continue to be paid, and that customer orders will be filled promptly. Alliance is seeking to restructure about $322 million of long-term debt and revolving credit and $204.1 million in trade and similar obligations as of May 31.
"Alliance's growth through acquisition resulted in the accumulation of burdensome levels of debt and interest expense at a time of little or no growth in the domestic music industry," said Teller.

The company is in talks to sell its Red Ant unit, a Los Angeles-based new release product label specialising in alternative rock and urban music, which Alliance bought from its principals, Teller and investment firm Wasserstein Perella in August 1996, when Teller was named head of Alliance.
Alliance received a preliminary proposal for consideration with respect to a $50 million equity investment in connection with a reorganization plan.
It has entered a loan agreement with a syndicate of banks led by Chase Manhattan Corp. that provides for about $50 million of debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing.
The company requested court approval to use $3 million in cash collateral pending interim approval of the DIP financing, which is expected to be approved by the court as early as Wednesday.
The company said the $50 million financing will allow the filing entities to continue operations uninterrupted, purchase new goods, and improve operating margins.

Beside Red Ant, Alliance excluded from the Chapter 11 filing Castle Communications, the British-based catalogue and re-issue label, and St. Clair Entertainment Group, its Canadian subsidiary. Both businesses are also part of the proprietary products group.
The company said the exclusion of Castle and St. Clair was related to their status as non-domestic entities.
